t: Notwithstanding section 1101, the level for “Social Security Administration, Supplemental Security Income Program” for research and demonstrations under sections 1110, 1115, and 1144 of the Social Security Act shall be $17,000,000.

fable.w: This provision only sets an appropriations funding level for research and demonstrations under the Social Security Act. The tempting reading is that research and demonstration projects might involve outside parties, but the text itself requires no consultation, comment, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue. No party outside the federal government is brought into any federal decision.
fable.s: the level for “Social Security Administration, Supplemental Security Income Program” for research and demonstrations under sections 1110, 1115, and 1144 of the Social Security Act shall be $17,000,000

qwen_block.w: This section sets a specific funding cap for a federal program. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or interaction with parties outside the federal government. There are no advisory boards, public comment periods, or requirements to consult with states or the public mentioned in this text.
qwen_block.s: Notwithstanding section 1101, the level for “Social Security Administration, Supplemental Security Income Program” for research and demonstrations under sections 1110, 1115, and 1144 of the Social Security Act shall be $17,000,000.

opus.w: This is an appropriations provision that sets the funding level for SSI research and demonstrations. It sets up no process for outside parties to consult with or take part in a federal decision. The mention of 'demonstrations' and cross-referenced sections that could involve outside entities is not enough, because this text itself creates no participation mechanism.
opus.s: the level for “Social Security Administration, Supplemental Security Income Program” for research and demonstrations under sections 1110, 1115, and 1144 of the Social Security Act shall be $17,000,000.
opus.b: Someone might be tempted to say Yes because sections 1110, 1115, and 1144 of the Social Security Act cover research, demonstration projects, and outreach that can involve states or outside groups. But this section only sets a funding level. It creates no consultation, hearing, advisory body, comment period, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government.
